title: Modern C++ Templates & Language Features
summary: Quick revision of C++ templates, type deduction (auto/decltype), range-for, structured bindings, constexpr, optional/variant, C++20 concepts, and what each standard from C++11 to C++20 added.

chapters.title: Modern C++ Handbook Overview
points: Function and class templates
auto and decltype
Range-for and structured bindings
constexpr
optional and variant
Concepts (C++20)

chapters.title: Function and Class Templates
points: Template is a compile-time blueprint: `template<typename T> T max(T a, T b)` is instantiated per distinct T, so each type gets its own generated code
Function templates deduce T from arguments (`max(1, 2)` gives int); `max(1, 2.5)` fails because T conflicts, so write `max<double>(1, 2.5)`
Class templates need explicit args before C++17 (`std::vector<int>`); C++17 CTAD deduces them: `std::pair p{1, 'a'}`
Full specialization `template<> struct S<int>{}` replaces one type; function templates cannot be partially specialized, so use overloads or `if constexpr`
Mistake: template definitions must be visible in the header, otherwise the linker reports undefined references; also `typename T::value_type` needs `typename` for dependent names

chapters.title: auto, decltype and Range-for
points: `auto x = expr` deduces the type from the initializer and drops top-level const and references: `const int& r` becomes `int`
`auto&` keeps the reference and const; `const auto&` binds to anything without copying; `auto&&` is a forwarding reference
`decltype(expr)` gives the exact declared type, keeping const and references; `decltype((x))` with double parentheses gives `T&`
`decltype(auto)` (C++14) returns with decltype rules, so `decltype(auto) f() { return (x); }` returns a reference, a dangling-reference risk
Range-for `for (const auto& e : v)` avoids copies; plain `for (auto e : v)` copies each element, and `auto&` on `vector<bool>` fails because its proxy is a temporary

chapters.title: Structured Bindings and constexpr
points: Structured bindings (C++17) unpack pairs, tuples, arrays and aggregates: `auto [it, ok] = m.insert({k, v});`
Bind by reference to modify the source: `for (auto& [key, val] : map) val++;` while plain `auto [a, b]` copies the object
`constexpr` variables are compile-time constants usable as array sizes and template arguments: `constexpr int N = 4; int a[N];`
`constexpr` functions may run at compile time or run time; `consteval` (C++20) forces compile time and `constinit` guarantees static initialization
Mistake: structured-binding names cannot be captured by lambdas before C++20, and `constexpr` is not the same as `const`, since const may be initialized at run time

chapters.title: optional and variant
points: `std::optional<T>` (C++17) holds a T or nothing: `if (o) use(*o);` and `o.value_or(0)` supplies a default
`o.value()` throws `bad_optional_access` when empty, while `*o` on an empty optional is undefined behaviour
`std::variant<int, string>` holds exactly one alternative: `std::get<int>(v)` throws `bad_variant_access` on a wrong type, and `std::get_if<int>(&v)` returns nullptr instead
`std::visit` dispatches on the active type: `std::visit(overloaded{[](int){}, [](string){}}, v)` must cover every alternative or it fails to compile

Choose optional for a value that may be absent, variant for a closed set of types, and a sentinel or pointer for neither; a default-constructed variant holds its first type, so use `std::monostate` first if that type is not default-constructible

chapters.title: Concepts and C++ Standards Cheatsheet
points: Concept (C++20): `template<typename T> concept Number = std::is_arithmetic_v<T>;` names a compile-time constraint
Use it as `template<Number T>`, `void f(Number auto x)`, or `requires Number<T>`; failures give a readable error instead of pages of template noise
requires expression checks syntax: `requires(T a) { a + a; { a.size() } -> std::convertible_to<size_t>; }`
C++11: auto, decltype, range-for, lambdas, move semantics, constexpr, nullptr, smart pointers. C++14: generic lambdas, decltype(auto), return-type deduction
C++17: structured bindings, CTAD, if constexpr, optional, variant, string_view. C++20: concepts, ranges, coroutines, modules, consteval, three-way operator <=>
